series.name: 3000 BCE
series.tagline: Ancient power. Modern playbook. Same game.
series.concept: Indian mythology told as modern thriller. Mahabharat as boardroom politics. Lanka as tech empire. Draupadi's court as a harassment tribunal. Krishna as a fixer. Each episode is one scene, one twist. The mythology is real -- the framing is modern. Every episode ends with a modern parallel. Not retelling mythology. Revealing it was always about power, betrayal, ambition, justice, and the people destroyed by all four.

episodes.title: The Boardroom

slides.text: Dhritarashtra sat at the head of the table. Blind since birth. Chairman of Hastinapur Corp since his brother Pandu died. He built nothing. Inherited everything. The board respected his name. Not his judgment. He knew it. That's why he overcompensated with the one thing he could control: his son's future.

Duryodhan walked into every room like he owned it. He didn't. Not yet. But his father was about to fix that. The Pandav division was outperforming every metric. Duryodhan's was bleeding. The numbers didn't matter. The surname did.

'Effective immediately, my son Duryodhan will serve as CEO.' Bhishma -- oldest director, the man who kept the company alive for three generations -- closed his laptop. He'd seen this before. Family destroying what merit built.

The Pandavs weren't in the room. Nobody told them. Yudhishthir found out from a WhatsApp forward. Not even a direct message. A forward. That's how they learned their company was stolen. Not with a sword. With a board resolution.

3000 BCE: A blind king gives his throne to his undeserving son. 2026: A founder's son gets the CEO role over performing executives. The playbook hasn't changed in 5,000 years. Nepotism doesn't need a kingdom. It just needs a boardroom.

episodes.synopsis: Dhritarashtra, blind chairman, gives his unqualified son Duryodhan the CEO role over the performing Pandav division. The first betrayal is in a corner office.
episodes.caption: A blind chairman gives his failing son the CEO role. The cousins find out from a WhatsApp forward. 3000 BCE or 2026? Nepotism looks the same in every century.

episodes.title: The Exile

slides.text: Duryodhan didn't fire his cousins. 'Incredible opportunity in Varnavat. Full autonomy.' Everything too generous. When the deal is too good, you're the product.
Beautiful new office. Every surface made of lac. Lightweight. Cheap. Flammable. One spark: ash. The architect was on payroll.
Vidura called. One proverb: 'The man who leaves the burning house survives.' Yudhishthir understood. The building was a trap.
Bheem dug a tunnel. Weeks. The night the fire was set, they were underground. News: 'Five dead.' The bodies were mannequins.
A palace of lac then. A golden handshake now. If the opportunity looks too perfect, ask: who benefits from your absence?

episodes.synopsis: Pandavs sent to a subsidiary in Varnavat -- a building made of flammable lac. Corporate restructuring meets attempted murder. They escape through a tunnel.
episodes.caption: Sent to a building made of fire fuel. Called it a promotion. The playbook: make the trap look like an opportunity. Still happens in every restructuring. Ask yourself: who benefits if you're gone?

episodes.title: The Swayamvar

slides.text: Build a working prototype in 24 hours. The prize wasn't Draupadi. She wasn't a prize. The prize was her approval. Without it, no deal.
Duryodhan. Karna. CEOs. One by one, failed. Draupadi's expression: bored. She'd seen ambition without ability her whole life.
A nobody. No suit. No badge. Eleven minutes. Not 24 hours. Eleven. Perfect prototype. 'Who are you?' 'Nobody important. Yet.'
Arjun. A Pandav. Officially dead. Duryodhan went white. Draupadi didn't react. She'd already decided. She chose competence in a room of entitlement. Not romance. Strategy.
The first pitch competition in history. The first investor who refused to be impressed by last names. 3000 BCE had VCs too.

episodes.synopsis: Draupadi's swayamvar as a tech pitch competition. She's the VC. Arjun solves the impossible challenge in 11 minutes. She chose competence over entitlement.
episodes.caption: A pitch competition. 5000 years ago. Draupadi wasn't the prize. She was the judge. A nobody solved it in 11 minutes. She chose competence. Not mythology. How the best VCs still work.

episodes.title: The Dice Game

slides.text: Shakuni's dice couldn't be lost. Yudhishthir lost the subsidiary. The shares. His brothers. His freedom. Each loss invited more. The psychology of gambling weaponized.
'One more thing. Draupadi.' The room went cold. And Yudhishthir agreed. He bet his wife. Like property. Like she was his to lose.
Dragged in by her hair. She didn't scream. One question: 'If he lost himself first, he had no right to bet me. The bet is illegal.' The room went silent. She was right.
Nobody answered. Not Bhishma. Not Drona. Not Yudhishthir. The most powerful men sat in silence. That silence created something. Not sadness. Rage.
'I will not tie my hair until it's washed in the blood of the men who did this.' Not a vow. A declaration of war.

A woman's autonomy gambled by a husband who thought he owned her. A room of powerful men who watched and said nothing. 2026: how many boardrooms have watched and stayed silent? Her question isn't mythology. It's every woman who asked 'who gave you the right?'

episodes.synopsis: Yudhishthir gambles the company, brothers, himself, then Draupadi in rigged dice. She asks one question that proves the bet was illegal. Nobody answers. She vows war.
episodes.caption: He bet his wife. She was dragged in. A room of powerful men watched. She asked one question that proved the bet was illegal. Nobody answered. She swore revenge. 3000 BCE or today? The silence sounds the same.

episodes.title: The Fixer

slides.text: They found Krishna in a tea shop. Eating butter. 'I've been expecting you.' 'How long?' '5,000 years. Give or take.' The most dangerous man looked like a dairy farmer.
'I don't fight. I drive. I advise. I arrange what needs to happen. One condition: I never lie. I also never tell the whole truth. Get comfortable with that.'
Not an army. A strategy for every enemy. 'Bhishma: can't be killed by a man. Drona: drops weapons at son's death. Karna: weak at sunset.' Every weakness known from understanding human nature.
'Why not end it?' 'I show the board. You move the pieces. Win by my hand and you lose yourselves. Know why you fight.' Philosophy weaponized.
The consultant who wins wars without fighting. McKinsey charges lakhs for this. The fixer is eternal. See the whole board, control the game.

episodes.synopsis: Krishna as consultant. Never fights, never lies, never tells whole truth. Knows every enemy's weakness from understanding human nature.
episodes.caption: Krishna doesn't fight. He drives. He advises. He knew every weakness from understanding people. The most dangerous man carried information, not a weapon. Sound familiar?

episodes.title: Five Villages

slides.text: 'Five villages. One per brother. That's all. This ends peacefully.' The simplest deal in history.
'I will not give them land enough to fit a needle's point.' Not villages. Not acres. A needle's point. The most devastating wars start with the smallest refusals.
Krishna stood. 'See you on the field.' As he walked out, the room felt him grow. For one second, they saw what he really was. Something vast.
A war started because one man wouldn't share a needle's worth. Billion-dollar lawsuits over patents and pride. Wars start over what someone refused to give when giving cost nothing.

episodes.synopsis: Krishna offers Duryodhan five villages for five brothers. He refuses to give even a needle's point. The moment war became inevitable.
episodes.caption: Five villages. That's all. He refused to give land the size of a needle's point. A war that killed millions started because one ego couldn't share a pinprick. How many lives destroyed over what could've been given for free?

episodes.title: The Talk

slides.text: Between two armies. 1.8 million soldiers. Arjun saw his grandfather. His teacher. Dropped his bow. 'I'd rather die than win this way.'
'Detach from the outcome. Attach to your duty. The result is the universe's problem. The action is yours.' The Gita in four sentences.
'I am time. The destroyer of worlds. They're already dead. You're the instrument.' Arjun picked up his bow.
The Gita isn't about war. It's about doing what's right when every reason says don't. Every founder. Every whistleblower. Every person who stood up.

episodes.synopsis: Arjun freezes. His enemies are family. Krishna delivers the Gita: detach from outcome, attach to duty. Then reveals his cosmic form. Arjun picks up his bow.
episodes.caption: Between two armies, the greatest warrior froze. What Krishna told him became the most quoted philosophy ever: do your duty. Detach from the result. You can't control the outcome. You can control whether you showed up.

episodes.title: The Fall of Bhishma

slides.text: Ten days. 10,000 a day. He chose when to die. How do you defeat someone who can only be beaten by choice?
Bhishma won't fight Shikhandi. Place Shikhandi in front. Arjun fires from behind. Not a lie. Not fair. How wars are won.
He fell on a bed of arrows. Chose to wait until war ended. Even in defeat, he controlled his exit.
Integrity becomes a weakness when others have none. The corporate world calls it leverage. History calls it tragedy.

episodes.synopsis: Bhishma can't be killed in fair combat. Krishna's solution: Shikhandi as shield, Arjun fires from behind. Fairness dies on Day 10.
episodes.caption: Bhishma: brought down by his own principles. He wouldn't fight. They shot from behind. Fairness died on Day 10. The person with the most integrity is always the most vulnerable.

episodes.title: The Lie That Killed a Teacher

slides.text: Kill an elephant named Ashwatthama. Tell Drona. Technically true. The only voice Drona trusts: Yudhishthir. The honest man delivering a dishonest message.
'Ashwatthama is dead... the elephant.' Krishna blew a conch. The last words drowned. Drona heard only death.
Weapons dropped. Eyes closed. Meditating in battle. Beheaded unarmed. The teacher died believing a lie from his most trusted student.
Half-truths don't need lies. Just the right truth at the wrong time. The conch is now an algorithm. The half-truth is now a headline.

episodes.synopsis: Drona killed by a half-truth: 'Ashwatthama is dead' -- the elephant. Yudhishthir delivers it. Krishna's conch drowns the qualifier. The first post-truth moment.
episodes.caption: Told his son was dead. Technically an elephant's name. The honest man delivered it. A conch drowned the truth. The first post-truth moment. 5000 years. Haven't learned.

episodes.title: Karna

slides.text: Greatest warrior. Better than Arjun. Everyone knew. Nobody said it. Born wrong. Raised low. Highest talent. Lowest ceiling. Never seen as equal.
Aim fails at worst moment. Earth swallows chariot wheel. Promised to spare four brothers. Three curses. None his fault. All fatal.
Chariot wheel sank. Asked for a pause. Arjun hesitated. Krishna: 'Where was their code for Abhimanyu? For Draupadi? Shoot.' The arrow flew.
His last thought: 'At least Arjun pulled the string.' Even dying, he wanted to lose to skill, not fate.
Talent without access. Merit without network. The wrong ZIP code. Karna is everyone the system wasn't designed for.

episodes.synopsis: The outsider. Better than Arjun. Three curses, none his fault. Died pulling a stuck wheel while rules were suspended for everyone except him.
episodes.caption: Karna. Greatest warrior. Born wrong. Three curses, none earned. Died pulling a stuck wheel. 5000 years and we still punish people for where they started instead of what they built.

episodes.title: Gandhari's Curse

slides.text: Blindfolded since marriage. Raised 100 sons blind. Now standing over their bodies. A mother counts bodies by grief alone.
'Your Yadavs will destroy themselves. You'll die alone. Shot by a hunter.' Krishna: 'Tathastu.' Accepted.
Years later, Yadavs killed each other. Krishna died in a forest, shot by a hunter. The most powerful being died of a mother's words. Grief is the one force even gods can't outmaneuver.
The architect destroyed by his own collateral. Every leader who burns people discovers they don't forget. The bill always comes.

episodes.synopsis: Gandhari lost 100 sons. Curses Krishna: your clan will destroy itself. You'll die alone. He accepts: 'Tathastu.' The curse fulfills.
episodes.caption: 100 sons dead. She cursed Krishna. It worked. His clan destroyed itself. He died alone. Even gods answer to a mother's grief. The collateral always sends the bill.

episodes.title: The Empire of Lanka

slides.text: Ten areas of mastery. Built Lanka from nothing. Golden city. Self-driving chariots. Aerial vehicles. Not a demon. A genius.
So smart he confused intelligence with entitlement. Believed he deserved everything. Including a woman who said no. Intelligence without humility: the most dangerous kind.
Months in the garden. Throne offered. Refused. Threats. Refused. She wasn't waiting for rescue. Her 'no' was more powerful than his empire.
A genius destroyed by one 'no.' How many empires have fallen because power couldn't accept rejection?

episodes.synopsis: Ravan: ten areas of mastery. Built the most advanced city. Fell because he couldn't accept one 'no' from one woman. Intelligence without humility.
episodes.caption: Ravan built the most advanced civilization. Ten fields mastered. Fell because he couldn't accept one 'no.' Intelligence without humility. Power without consent. The smartest person who couldn't hear the simplest word.

episodes.title: The Bridge

slides.text: No army. No navy. An ocean. Just Vanars -- dismissed as animals. Nobody wanted them. They built a bridge across the ocean in five days.
Flew to Lanka alone. Found Sita. Burned half the city. Came back. Went to being a soldier. The most powerful chose to serve. The rarest strength.
Ram's arrow: not the head, not the heart. The navel. Hidden weakness. Strategy over strength. Always.
Outcasts crossing oceans. Nobody teams beating empires. The bridge is the playbook for every team of nobodies who said: let's build.

episodes.synopsis: Ram has no army. Just Vanars -- forest dwellers nobody wanted. They build a bridge across an ocean. The greatest engineering feat by the most dismissed people.
episodes.caption: A bridge across an ocean. Built by people nobody wanted. An empire of genius defeated by an army of outcasts. Align nobodies behind a mission: impossible becomes inevitable.

episodes.title: The Fire

slides.text: 'The people will doubt your purity. Walk through fire.' Not 'I doubt you.' 'The people will.' Hiding cowardice behind public opinion. The oldest excuse.
She walked in furious. Fire parted. Agni refused to burn her. She passed. The real test was Ram's. He failed when he asked.
'You chose their doubt over my dignity. Protected your throne, not me.' The most powerful exit line in mythology.
Banished again. She called to the earth. It opened. She descended with dignity. Sometimes the most powerful thing is to leave.

episodes.synopsis: Ram demands Agni Pariksha. Sita walks through fire untouched. Tells Ram: you protected your throne, not me. Later, she chooses the earth over his kingdom.
episodes.caption: Walked through fire. Untouched. Told Ram: you protected your throne, not me. When tested again, she chose the earth over his kingdom. The first walkout. The first woman who decided: I'd rather disappear than keep proving myself.

episodes.title: The Throne of Ashes

slides.text: Crowned king. Won through a lie, a loophole, a rigged kill. He walked the battlefield. 1.66 billion dead. He won. It felt like the biggest loss.
'Was it worth it?' Krishna didn't smile. 'Wrong question. Rule for the widows and orphans. The survivors. That's the only meaning.'
Years later. Walked to heaven. Brothers fell. At the gates: Duryodhan in heaven. Brothers in hell. 'Send me to hell with my family.' He passed. By choosing love over paradise.
Victory without purpose: organized destruction with a trophy. The final test wasn't power. It was what you give up for the people you love. Still the only test.

episodes.synopsis: Yudhishthir wins. Takes the throne. Realizes he rules over corpses. Eventually walks to heaven and chooses hell with family over paradise alone.
episodes.caption: He won. Counted the dead. Gave up the throne. At heaven's gates, chose hell with family over paradise alone. After 5000 years, that's still the only test: what will you give up for the people you love?

episodes.title: Eklavya's Thumb

slides.text: Drona refused: wrong caste. Eklavya taught himself in front of a mud statue. Became better than Arjun. Without permission.
'Give me your thumb.' Without it, he can never shoot again. The teacher didn't lift the student. He cut him down.
Every scholarship denied. Every talent suppressed. Every 'not the right fit.' Eklavya's thumb is every glass ceiling.

episodes.synopsis: Self-taught. Better than Arjun. Teacher demanded his thumb to protect the favorite. He cut it off. Smiling. The most brutal gatekeeping.
episodes.caption: Self-taught. Better than everyone. Reward: his teacher demanded his thumb. To protect a richer student. 5000 years and we're still demanding thumbs from people who dared to be better than the system allowed.

episodes.title: The Boy in the Maze

slides.text: Learned entry in the womb. Mother fell asleep before exit. Born with half the tools. Enough to enter. Not enough to leave.
'I can get in. Can't get out.' They sent him anyway. The old send the young to die for their mistakes.
Bow broken: chariot wheel. Wheel broken: fists. Seven couldn't beat him one on one. He fell. Sixteen. The war's most cowardly act.
Every young person sent into a broken system. Given half the tools. Told to figure it out. Abhimanyu is every kid carrying adult failures.

episodes.synopsis: Abhimanyu: 16, knows entry not exit. Sent into the Chakravyuha anyway. Seven warriors kill one boy. The war's most unforgivable moment.
episodes.caption: Sixteen. Half the knowledge. Sent in anyway. Seven grown warriors killed one boy. The adults who should have protected him sent him to die. Still sacrificing the young for the failures of the old.

episodes.title: The Queen Who Was Owed

slides.text: Before exile, she was a warrior. Held a chariot axle with bare hands in battle. Saved the king. Two boons promised. He meant it then.
'Crown my son. Exile Ram.' The kingdom called her evil. She was calling in a debt. He honored it and blamed her. The oldest move: honor the deal, blame the negotiator.
A woman held a man to his word. History called her evil. A man negotiating is a leader. A woman: aggressive. The world hasn't forgiven women for holding men accountable.

episodes.synopsis: Kaikeyi saved the king's life. He promised boons. She collected: exile Ram, crown Bharat. History calls her villain. She was holding a man to his word.
episodes.caption: She saved his life. He promised anything. She collected. History calls her villain. She was a warrior calling in a debt. Why does a man's broken promise make a woman the villain? Still asking.

episodes.title: The Defector

slides.text: Told Ravan three times: return Sita. Private. Respectful. Ignore, mock, exile. He tried internal first. When internal fails, external becomes necessary.
Walked into Ram's camp alone. 'A man who leaves gold for principle has proven his worth.' Refuge given. Not everyone agreed.
Every whistleblower. Every employee who reported their company. Speak up. Lose everything. Called traitor by the people you tried to save.

episodes.synopsis: Vibhishan warned Ravan three times. Got exiled. Crossed to Ram. Every whistleblower knows this: speak up, lose everything, get called traitor by the people you tried to save.
episodes.caption: Warned his brother three times. Exiled. Crossed sides. Traitor or hero? Every whistleblower knows: you try to save the ship. They throw you overboard. Then it sinks.

episodes.title: The Secret

slides.text: Sixteen. Unmarried. A baby. Basket on a river. He grew up poor. Wrong caste. His mother watched from a palace. Saying nothing.
One sentence would have stopped the war: 'He's your brother.' She never said it. Reputation won. Truth lost. War became inevitable.
Every family built on unspoken truths. Every crisis from comfortable silence. Kunti's secret is every truth easier to hide than face.

episodes.synopsis: Kunti had Karna before marriage. Abandoned him. Watched him fight her other sons. One truth would have prevented the war. She chose reputation.
episodes.caption: She had a son. Abandoned him. Watched him become her other sons' enemy. One truth prevents the war. She chose reputation. Millions died. How many disasters start with a truth someone was too comfortable to tell?

episodes.title: The Forgotten Wife

slides.text: Met in a forest. Married. Promised to send for her. Left. Months. Nothing. Pregnant. Alone. No witnesses. No proof.
'I don't know this woman.' In front of his court. A curse, the story says. Curses are convenient when truth is uncomfortable.
'Your conscience knows. The trees heard. The fire heard. Your son's face is proof.' The most powerful testimony in mythology.

episodes.synopsis: Dushyant married Shakuntala. Left. 'Forgot.' She showed up at his court with his son. He denied her. She delivered the most powerful speech about selective memory.
episodes.caption: Married her. Left. 'Forgot.' She walked in with his son. He denied her. She told him: your conscience knows. Your son's face is proof. 5000 years. Men still conveniently forget.

episodes.title: The Women

slides.text: Named after men. Powered by women. Draupadi's rage started the war. Sita's abduction triggered another. Gandhari's curse ended a dynasty. The stories belong to the women.
Draupadi stopped a courtroom. Sita shamed a king. Gandhari cursed a god. Men had swords. Women had words. The words lasted longer.
Still tested. Still forgotten. Still gambled. Mythology didn't predict the future. It documented a permanent present.

episodes.synopsis: Draupadi's rage. Sita's dignity. Gandhari's grief. Kunti's silence. Kaikeyi's debt. The mythology belongs to the women who bore the weight.
episodes.caption: Named after men. Powered by women. Every epic. Draupadi's rage. Sita's dignity. Gandhari's grief. They weren't characters. They were the story. 5000 years later: less fiction, more mirror.

episodes.title: The Immortal

slides.text: War over. Entered sleeping camp. Killed five children. In revenge for a father killed by a lie. Answered dishonor with dishonor.
'You'll outlive everything. Including forgiveness.' Eternal wound. Can't die. Can't rest. Can't forget. Immortality as torture.
Guilt immortalized. The 3 AM replay for eternity. Some punishments don't need death. Just memory. And endless time.

episodes.synopsis: Ashwatthama killed sleeping children. Cursed: immortality with eternal wound. Wanders forever. The myth that doesn't end.
episodes.caption: Killed sleeping children. Cursed: live forever with it. Eternal wound. Some temples say he visits. The myth that doesn't end because some mistakes shouldn't be allowed to die.

episodes.title: No Heroes

slides.text: Yudhishthir lied to kill his teacher. Ram made his wife walk through fire. Krishna engineered deaths through loopholes. No heroes. Only humans with 5000-year consequences.
Duryodhan: product of overcompensation. Ravan: genius. Karna: loyal to the only side that accepted him. Villains aren't born. Made by the same world.
Not a morality tale. A mirror. Yudhishthir is the honest person who compromises once. Karna is the outsider. Draupadi is every silenced woman. Which character are you?
Every boardroom has a Duryodhan. Every team a Karna. Every family a Kunti. Gods optional. Humans eternal.

episodes.synopsis: No clean heroes. Yudhishthir lied. Ram failed. Krishna manipulated. Karna chose wrong side for right reasons. Not good vs evil. Human vs human.
episodes.caption: No heroes. No villains. Just humans. The mythology survived 5000 years because it wasn't about gods. It was about us. Still is.

episodes.title: Still Playing

slides.text: The dice game never ended. Palace to boardroom. Gold dice to stock options. Someone is always gambling someone else's life. Still playing.
You know a Duryodhan. A Karna. A Draupadi. A Bhishma. The mythology is your WhatsApp group.
Which one are you? The one gambling? Watching? Being gambled? The one who could stop it but won't? Recognize yourself. That's scarier than any demon.
You also know a Ram. A Hanuman. A Vibhishan. Not just warnings. Blueprints. For bridges. For standing up. For walking through fire. Choose your story.
5000 years. Still rolling dice. Still building bridges. Still asking the question. The mythology isn't history. It's a live feed. You're in it right now. Play wisely.

episodes.synopsis: The dice game never ended. The bridge is still being built. The thumbs are still demanded. 3000 BCE isn't a date. It's a mirror. You're in it.
episodes.caption: The dice game is still going. The bridge is still being built. The thumbs still demanded. 3000 BCE isn't a date. It's a mirror. You're in the mythology right now. Choose what happens next.
